series: Why we stop doing things we know are good for us, Reason #15 (the daily decision)
hook: If you have to decide to do it, one day you'll decide not to.

gate.goal_link: keeps the daily steps of any goal going past week one
gate.mechanism: a daily yes/no is a repeated bet: 0.9^7 = 48%, 0.9^30 = 4% chance of an unbroken month (real arithmetic)
gate.universal: everyone 'decides' each day whether to work out, read, practise

frame.mistake: deciding each day whether to do it
frame.cost: 9 wins in 10 still leaves a 4% chance of an unbroken month
frame.fix: one if-then sentence anchored to an existing habit (implementation intention)

hooks_considered.line: If you have to decide to do it, one day you'll decide not to.

hooks_considered.line: Winning 9 days out of 10 still breaks your habit.
Your habit has to win an argument every single day.
After a month, there's a 4% chance you never skipped.
Discipline isn't deciding well. It's deciding once.
